# I'm AiDog

> Your loyal AI companion — a personal embodied AI: a constitution for a personality, curated memory for a life, and a self-developed core that answers to you alone. Permanently free for any use, local-first console, 9-route channel gateway with Telegram live.

I'm AiDog is a single companion you run yourself — not a platform, not an assistant farm. Three constitutional facts: it is permanently free (no paid tier, no usage fee, no paid feature gate, ever), the console is local-first (state, memory and configuration stay on your own machine), and the core kernel is self-developed in-house rather than wrapped from a third party.

## Product

- Permanently free: no pricing, no paid features, no usage metering.
- Anonymous usage reporting: opt-in and OFF by default, one report per day per install (model name, request counts and token totals — never prompts, files, paths or credentials), switchable off in Settings; the Models section chart renders the public aggregates.
- Local-first console: web UI on your own machine for chat, memory, skills, cron and channel configuration.
- Platforms: Linux via `install.sh` (the reference path, WSL2 included), Windows through WSL2, macOS verified on arm64 (Miniconda + conda tmux, 2026-11-12), and iOS/Android through the Telegram bot plus this site — the console binds loopback-only on a machine you control, so remote access is an SSH tunnel, never a cloud console.
- Constitution and curated memory: behavioural rules and long-term memory are versioned assets you control — bounded Markdown budgets, archive tiers, a user-profile layer, no vector store you cannot read.
- Skills and automations: SKILL.md packs screened by a deterministic pre-router (route suite 37/37), natural-language cron that stays fail-closed until enabled, and a self-evolution loop (`/learn`, `/reflect`) with lint-gated writes.
- Channels: Telegram live, plus nine adapters (Discord / Slack / Email / Webhook / DingTalk / Feishu / WeChat / WhatsApp / Signal) each with an honest per-route status; unconfigured routes stay silent.
- Media: local speech-to-text voice sessions with fuzzy wake phrases, TTS announcements, BYOK image generation, Telegram photo send.
- Bring-your-own model: model endpoints and credentials are configured by the operator; zero-key trial path, upstream failover, budget caps.
- Desktop, profiles, ops: an Electron HUD shell (desktop suite 23/23), fully isolated multi-profiles (isolation gate 63/63), `aidog doctor` health checks (0 FAIL · 0 WARN), watchdog and one-command upgrades.
- Web3 exchanges: nine venues in one catalog — keyless chain reads (Jupiter, Velora, Hyperliquid, dYdX, GMX, public RPC) beside slot-gated CEX accounts (OKX, Kraken, Binance) behind six `exchange_*` tools. Orders only ever run prepare → human console approval → execute; thresholds fail closed (default 0 = every plan waits for a person), market orders never auto-approve, and withdrawals / on-chain transfers / transaction signing do not exist in the core at all. With no slot configured the order tool never registers.
- Activation & operations: the console's Overview ACTIVATION card mirrors `aidog setup --check` (required slots, endpoint reachability, service state) with FIX deep-links; a credential-slot editor writes runtime slots with values never echoed; doctor-run, service-restart and update controls live in the panel.
- Skills ecosystem: an official skills directory at https://aidog.im/skills.html backed by a public,
  lint-and-review gated skills repository; `GET /api/skills/remote` serves the same catalog fail-soft
  (remote -> bundled copy -> honest `unavailable`, never a 5xx).
- Evidence (the same numbers shown in the site's fact strip): core tests 2494/2494 · console smoke 558/558 · skill router 37/37 · memory 58/58 · setup wizard 123/123 · profile isolation 63/63 · desktop shell 23/23 · doctor 0 FAIL · 0 WARN · 28 real-machine E2E suites · 1555 locale keys per pack · 29 registered tools · 37 capability documents · 40 self-developed modules ≈ 24.5k LOC.
- Current release: 0.5.88.

## Interfaces

- Web console: streaming chat UI plus settings, memory, cron, skills and channel management on `127.0.0.1`.
- Telegram bot: first-class messaging channel with streaming replies and typing indicators.
- OpenAI-compatible API: the local console exposes `GET /v1/models` and `POST /v1/chat/completions` (streaming and non-streaming) behind a Bearer token, so OpenAI-style tooling can point at it.
- Console ops endpoints (loopback): `GET /api/setup` (readiness rows, presence/format words only), `POST /api/doctor/run`, `POST /api/service/restart`, `POST /api/update/apply`, `GET /api/version` — every write behind the Bearer token, no value ever serialized.

## Live stats

- [Usage stats](https://aidog.im/api/stats): public aggregates over the anonymous daily usage ledger — installs, requests, token totals, the last seven UTC days and per-model / per-scenario breakdowns. Each install reports once per UTC day; reports carry model names and counts only — never prompts, files, paths or credentials — and verification canary rows (ids starting with `_`) are stored but never aggregated. The `install_id` is a random per-install pseudonym, not a device or account fingerprint; deleting its state file resets it. If the ledger is not configured the endpoint answers `503` with an error object instead of a fabricated zero.
- [Visits](https://aidog.im/api/visits): JSON counter returning `{"count": <integer>, "unit": "page views", "note": "approximate, includes crawlers and refreshes"}`. One increment per page load; approximate by design. Append `?format=text` for `text/plain` output (`visits: <integer>`). If the counter is not configured the endpoint answers `503` with an error object instead of a fabricated number.

## Links

- [Home](https://aidog.im/#home): positioning and facts.
- [Start](https://aidog.im/#start): install and first-run commands.
- [Skills](https://aidog.im/#skills): what the skill system does.
- [Skills directory](https://aidog.im/skills): the official, review-gated skill catalog (six categories, bilingual).
- [Capabilities](https://aidog.im/#capabilities): the card-by-card feature inventory, including the Web3 approval gate.
- [Sniff](https://aidog.im/#sniff): the read-only sense engine that sweeps, finds and speaks first.
- [Console](https://aidog.im/#console): the local-first web console.
- [Models](https://aidog.im/#models): model configuration.
- [Usage statistics](https://aidog.im/models): the full statistics page — all-time totals, the last seven UTC days, and the per-model / per-scenario breakdowns rendered from the same public `/api/stats` endpoint.
- [Security](https://aidog.im/#security): credential discipline and approval gates.
- [Architecture](https://aidog.im/#architecture): kernel / body / business layer separation.
- [Documentation](https://aidog.im/docs): the documentation center — Telegram command reference, every capability document and the guides.
- [Agent instructions](https://aidog.im/agents.md): what this site is, its public API, and its machine-readable surfaces.
- [OpenAPI spec](https://aidog.im/openapi.json): OpenAPI 3.1 description of the public site API.
- [GitHub](https://github.com/AiDog-im/AiDog): source repository.
- [robots.txt](https://aidog.im/robots.txt) · [Sitemap](https://aidog.im/sitemap.xml) · [manifest](https://aidog.im/manifest.webmanifest)

homepage.body:
AIDOG.IM
Home Start Skills Capabilities Desktop Sniff Console Models Security Architecture Docs
GitHub

PERSONAL · EMBODIED · LOCAL-FIRST

I'm AiDoggrown for one, built for anyone

Your loyal AI companion

A personal AI that runs on your own machine: talk to it from a channel you choose — Telegram, Feishu, DingTalk — or the console, it remembers what matters, and it keeps the jobs you scheduled.

Not a platform. Not an assistant farm. One companion grown for one person — a constitution for a personality, curated memory for a life, a self-developed core that answers to you alone.

PERMANENTLY FREE — forever, no exceptions Self-developed core · 40 modules · 2494/2494 tests Runs on your machine · loopback by default
Get Started View on GitHub
keeping watch
2494/2494 core tests 40 self-developed modules 558/558 console smoke 37/37 skill router 58/58 memory suite 0F/0W doctor check 28 real-machine E2E suites 123/123 setup wizard 63/63 profile isolation 23/23 desktop shell 29 registered tools 37 capability docs ≈24.5k lines of core code 1555 locale keys · en + zh each
The engraved watch

Four marks on one continuous line.

Your loyal AI companion

Most assistants begin when you speak. AiDog begins by holding context — then noticing, weighing, preparing, and stopping where your authority starts.

01 / SENSE

Read the room

Heartbeats, memory, releases, cost — the signals that belong to your world, gathered without you asking.

02 / COUNSEL

Know which changes matter

Most drift is noise. The rare ones arrive with a reason, a severity, and a sentence you can act on.

03 / PROTOCOL

Prepare a reversible move

A diff, a plan, a way back. Prepared in full, executed by no one until you say so.

04 / RECOVER

Stay yourself, anywhere

Constitution, memory and skills travel with you. No single machine gets to hold your dog hostage.

01

Get Started

From zero to a running console in three steps. What you need first: Linux, or Windows through WSL2, with Python 3.10+, tmux and git — plus two things only you can bring: a model endpoint and a chat-channel token (a Telegram bot, or any adapter you prefer).

1

Get the repository

I'm AiDog is public on GitHub — clone it with zero credentials.

git clone https://github.com/AiDog-im/AiDog.git aidog && cd aidog
▸
2

Run the installer

One command: provision + boot + verify. The installer is idempotent, so re-running it is always safe.

bash deploy/install.sh
▸
3

Fill the slots

The wizard asks for what only you have: a console token (any long random string you invent), a chat-channel token (a Telegram bot, or another route you prefer), who may talk to it, and where your model lives. A model key is optional — a local endpoint needs none. Values are hidden as you type and never echoed; the console's ACTIVATION card mirrors the same check, with a FIX deep-link on every failing row.

aidog setup

Then open http://127.0.0.1:19167 — the console is already running.

Full install guide — prerequisites, every slot, troubleshooting

Everything here is public today — clone the repository and run the installer. No waitlist, no sign-up key: releases are on GitHub.

02

Run it on the system you already own

The console runs on a machine you control — here is the honest platform matrix: what is tested, what is expected, and what each system actually gets.

Linux

One command with install.sh — the reference path, fully tested, including inside WSL2 on Windows.

Windows

Run the console inside WSL2 with the same command, then grab the portable Windows shell (zip, no installer) from the GitHub Release — it attaches to your WSL2 console on localhost; the shell itself is verified on Windows and Linux.

macOS

Python 3.10+, tmux and git — verified on macOS 26 (arm64), 2026-11-12: Miniconda supplies Python 3.10+ and `conda install -c conda-forge tmux` (no Homebrew, no sudo). GitHub blocked? take the codeload zip instead of cloning.

iOS / Android

Use a chat channel plus this website (installable to your home screen). The console binds to localhost on your own machine; reach it from a phone through an SSH tunnel — there is no cloud console, by design.

Read the installation guide on GitHub

03

Skills

A small, curated capability layer. Skills are screened deterministically before they ever reach the model, and only trusted, reviewed entries are recommended — no open marketplace, no supply-chain surprises.

Curation in progress

No recommended skills are listed yet on this page — but the official directory already ships curated, lint-screened, review-gated entries you can browse and install. Recommendations land here one by one as they pass review.

Browse the official skills directory

Curated on purpose — every entry passed a machine gate (structure, format, leak scan) and a human review. No marketplace, no surprise code.

See all in the skills directory Propose a skill on GitHub Issues
1

Submit

Publish your skill repository on GitHub and open an issue with the link and a short description of what it does.

▸
2

Review

We read the code: permissions, network behaviour, data handling. Skills must pass the deterministic router checks and our security review.

▸
3

Listed

Approved skills appear in the recommended shelf above and mount into your local install — read-only sources, revocable at any time.

04

Capabilities

What the product actually does, card by card — every line comes from the release gates and the capability docs, thirty-seven of them in the repository today, nothing invented.

Streaming chat everywhere

Console chat streams by SSE and Telegram replies stream behind a typing heartbeat, so an answer reaches you as it is written.

Voice sessions & media BYOK

Local speech-to-text sessions with fuzzy wake phrases, TTS announcements through your own engine key, BYOK image generation and Telegram photo send.

Skill workshop

Skills ship as SKILL.md with industry-standard frontmatter; the deterministic router picks the TOP3 candidates before any body loads — 37/37.

Two-layer memory

Curated long-term memory in bounded Markdown budgets with archive tiers, plus a user-profile layer — memory suite 58/58, no vector store you cannot read.

Natural-language cron & self-evolution

Schedule in plain language — /cron ship the report tomorrow 9am parses into a job that stays fail-closed until you enable it — while /learn and /reflect grow the loop behind lint-gated writes. Automatic evolution ships off; you switch it on.

9-route channel gateway

Telegram stands equal with nine adapters — Discord / Slack / Email / Webhook / DingTalk / Feishu / WeChat / WhatsApp / Signal — each reports an honest status and stays silent while unconfigured.

Desktop HUD shell

An Electron frameless shell with transparency slider, always-on-top and tray — Linux and Windows portable packaging verified (selftest green on both); macOS honestly not built yet; desktop suite 23/23.

Multi-profile isolation

AIDOG_PROFILE selects fully isolated profiles — settings, secrets, state and body kept apart — proven by a 63/63 isolation gate and an 18-leg real-machine E2E.

Terminal backends & code runs

The shell backend is grammar-checked local, Docker or SSH; execute_code folds into at most 8 steps with checkpointed file writes you can restore.

Subagents & MCP

Up to three isolated parallel delegates with fresh context, plus an MCP client for stdio and HTTP servers with tool allow/deny filtering.

Hooks & context files

Seven lifecycle events can run your own command on a timeout — the child gets only PATH and HOME, never a credential — and context dirs pull shared files into a turn.

OpenAI-compatible gateway

The loopback console exposes GET /v1/models and POST /v1/chat/completions — streaming and non-streaming — behind a Bearer token for OpenAI-style tooling.

Doesn't stop at the first failure

Multi-upstream failover with per-endpoint tests and rate caps, web fetch that can route through a relay you run yourself, and a model tier that moves on when an endpoint goes quiet — a dead endpoint costs a retry, not the night.

Runs while you sleep

Plain-language cron, missions with milestones and red lines, and a watchdog that keeps a 24/7 escalation journal — reaching you on Telegram once you give it a chat id. The schedule reads as a rhythm: every job shows its next-due time.

Always under your hand

A tail you can read — IDLE, WORKING, PAUSED, BUDGET HOLD — plus STOP and PAUSE on the Overview, daily budget guardrails, and rules and forbidden zones the constitution has to honour.

It keeps a memory of you

Beyond the tasks it keeps a profile of you — what you prefer, what you said matters — written and updated by the model itself and shown as a gauge in the console. A browsable view of it is next.

Extensions — one panel, three tabs

The console's Extensions panel opens three doors: keyless market quotes, your smart home, and your vehicle — the last two are thin paths into Sniff, observed read-only and never driven.

◇

Finance — quotes without a key

A-share and US quotes fetch with no credential at all, and the trading cockpit links out as an external tool. Orders keep the gate they have always had: prepare, approve, execute — nothing moves without your approval.

▸
◈

Smart home — observed, not driven

Home Assistant states and your own bridges are read through declared, read-only senses — GET only, never a service call. This tab is a door into the Sniff board.

▸
◉

Smart vehicle — the same nose

Vehicle signals ride the same read-only senses and land in the same findings log: again a path into Sniff, not a remote control.

Market data needs no credential, and with no slot configured the order tool never registers at all. Orders stay behind the human gate — prepare, approve, execute — while withdrawals, on-chain transfers and transaction signing do not exist in the core at all; the core suite asserts that absence against the source.

05

Desktop HUD — the console as a floating overlay

A frameless Electron shell that lifts the console onto your desktop: transparency slider, always-on-top, tray. It ships as a portable archive — no installer, no registry, no auto-update, no telemetry — and it attaches to the console you already run instead of spawning a second one.

Attaches, never spawns

The shell probes 127.0.0.1:19167 and attaches to your running console (set AIDOG_REPO when it cannot find the install). It never starts a second Python stack of its own.

Linux

Built (dir + tar.gz) and verified — the unpacked and the tar-extracted binary both run the shell's own --selftest green.

Windows

Portable zip on the GitHub Release: extract and run, then it attaches to your WSL2 console over localhost. Selftest-verified on Windows; unsigned by design.

macOS

The product itself runs on macOS (verified 2026-11-12); the macOS shell is not built yet — stated plainly rather than implied.

Download the portable shell Read the technical notes

06

Sniff — the nose that speaks first

A read-only sweep smells health, home, vehicle and web signals, turns them into findings with provenance, and speaks first only when one earns it.

Sniffing the room — the part of a dog that notices before you do.

◎

1 · Senses

A sweep reads only what it may read: Home Assistant states behind a bearer slot, one web page, or a declared bridge's configuration and session status. Never-configured stays silent; a source we did not reach is never called reachable.

▸
◇

2 · Sweeps

Bounded rules — no eval, a closed operator set, a sustain window — evaluate the readings the sweep just produced. A match becomes a durable, deduplicated finding in a local log your machine owns.

▸
◉

3 · Speaks first

Quiet hours, a digest cap, the global PAUSE and a per-rule speak flag decide whether a batch earns a message — delivered oldest-first through the same chain the cron lane uses.

home — Home Assistant

Entity states filtered by globs, the hub route for health sensors, locks and devices — GET only, never a service call.

web — one URL

A page hash plus an optional regex field, so a changed page or a crossed threshold becomes a reading instead of a guess.

mcp — borrowed bridges

Configuration and connection status of a bridge you run yourself — observed, never driven: no tool call, no spawned process, no connection of its own.

Use it in three steps

After install, open the Console → SENSE: add a source (a Home Assistant url + token slot, a URL + extract regex, or a bridge name from mycore.mcp), then add a rule like sensor.temp > 30 for 10m.

Hit SWEEP NOW (or wait out the interval): hits land in the FINDINGS timeline and stay on your machine — rules marked speak reach you first, with quiet hours, the digest cap and PAUSE deciding when.

Read-only by construction — no actuation path exists in the engine at all, and the suite asserts that absence. Personal signals stay on your machine, unconfigured sources never speak, and no paid tier ever touches them.

Get started

07

Console

Local Web Console Preview — see the panel you get after installing, before you download anything.

STATIC PREVIEW — live values render locally on your machine after install

A moment in the day

Quiet until it isn't.

A notification tells you something changed. The counsel tells you why it matters, what it would do, and where your say begins.

Preview only · no live service · nothing sent

Counsel · 09:14 Needs your word

Sir, the picture has shifted slightly.

Two deployment checks no longer match yesterday's baseline. The last release completed cleanly and no outage signal is present, so I have not treated this as urgent — but it will matter before your next deployment. I have prepared a review of the diff and a way back. Nothing has been sent, changed, or scheduled.

Awaitingyour authority
No action taken

Five panels, one glance

Status, settings, usage, events and voice — a situational console, not an admin warehouse.

Zero-dependency local server

Serves on 127.0.0.1 with plain standard library code; write operations require your local access token.

Channels + console, en/zh

Chat where you already are, inspect where it runs. Both faces speak English and Chinese.

Activation card in the Overview

The first Overview card mirrors the wizard's check — required slots, endpoint reachability, service state — and every failing row carries a FIX deep-link.

Credential-slot editor

37 runtime slots are editable from Settings; values are write-only and never echoed — output names slots and lengths.

Ops buttons, not a terminal

Run doctor, restart the chat service and apply an update from the panel; an upgrade banner appears the moment a newer release exists.

08

Models & Transparency

We will publish how this product actually runs — which models serve it and how much compute it consumes. No estimates, no marketing charts: only what the software itself reports.

STATISTICS LIVE — anonymous daily reports, aggregated in public.

The endpoint answers today: aggregate totals, the last seven days and per-model breakdowns, refreshed as each install reports once a day. Verification canary rows are stored but never aggregated, and no per-install record is ever published.

09

Security & Trust

Local-first by construction — the quiet guarantees, stated plainly.

Loopback by default

Services listen on 127.0.0.1 only — reachable from your machine, not from your network.

Credentials stay local

Secrets live in one gitignored file (mode 0600). Output and logs report slot names and lengths — never values.

Writes need your token

Every console write operation requires your local access token.

Anonymous reporting, opt-in (off by default)

Once a day the app sends model names and token totals to the public statistics — never prompts, files or credentials. Flip the switch in Settings and nothing leaves your machine.

en + zh interface, English source

The interface speaks English and Chinese; all source code is written in English.

Free forever

Permanently free — no paid tier, no in-app purchase, no usage fee, ever.

One passphrase, one file

Backup & Restore encrypts your credentials, settings and memory into a single .ckx file inside your browser — the passphrase never reaches the server. You can also schedule agent backups that re-run it on a timer you set, with a local call meter and a round-trip restore check.

It can be told off, and it keeps the correction

Rules and forbidden zones sit directly under the constitution. On any conflict the constitution wins, and the reply has to say which rule it did not apply.

Certificate of custody

What it may never do to you.

Power is only useful when you can see why it moved, stop it, and take it with you. These are not settings — they are the terms of the relationship.

Your credentialsnever echoed, anywhere
Consequential writeshuman approval required
Your memory & constitutionportable · recoverable
Your datalocal-first, loopback only

Free, permanently.

No paid tier, no usage fee, no feature gate. One dog, one owner — not a platform that grows to need your money.

Architecture

Three layers, strictly separated — so the core underneath can be swapped without losing who you are.

Kernel

The self-developed core runs today — 40 modules, ~24k LOC, zero upstream dependencies — and stays replaceable by design: swap the kernel, never swap 'me'.

▾

Body

Constitution · curated memory · skills · stance · persona — owned by this repo, independent of any kernel.

▾

Business

Chain access and project adapters — pure assets with no behaviour of their own.

The self-developed core is under active development — we publish what the gates prove, nothing more.

# Agents — aidog.im

This is the public site for **I'm AiDog**, a personal embodied AI you run
yourself: a constitution for a personality, curated memory for a life, and a
self-developed core that answers to you alone. Permanently free, local-first.

## Read first

- [llms.txt](llms.txt) — site map and product facts in Markdown.
- [llms-full.txt](llms-full.txt) — the full-length version.
- [Documentation](https://aidog.im/docs) — Telegram command reference, every
  capability document, and the installation guides.
- [openapi.json](openapi.json) — OpenAPI 3.1 spec for the public site API.

## Public API (no auth, aggregates only)

- `GET /api/stats` — usage aggregates (all-time totals, last seven UTC days,
  per-model / per-scenario breakdowns). Never a per-install record.
- `GET /api/visits` — approximate page-view counter.
- `POST /api/ledger` — one anonymous daily usage report per install
  (whitelist-exact schema; retries are idempotent).

## Machine-readable surfaces

- `/.well-known/mcp` — MCP endpoint declaration.
- `/robots.txt` — explicit allow for known AI crawlers (search, hybrid and
  training families) plus the sitemap reference.
- `/sitemap.xml` — page inventory with lastmod dates.

## Product in one paragraph

The console binds loopback-only on a machine you control; Telegram is the
first-class messaging channel; model endpoints and credentials are configured
by the operator (bring-your-own key). Orders in the Web3 exchange surface only
ever run prepare → human console approval → execute; withdrawals and on-chain
transfers do not exist in the core. Source: https://github.com/AiDog-im/AiDog

## Honesty notes

- Numbers on this site come from the release gates of the matching version —
  see `release.json` in the repository for the current one.
- Usage stats are opt-in, aggregated, and contain no prompts, files, paths or
  credentials.
